wordpressSecurity.alertText: On 21 October 2026, security fixes were released for two serious PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619). Not every WordPress site remains exposed, because many hosts have already patched their servers. This package pairs patch-status verification with a wider WordPress maintenance review.
wordpressSecurity.whyTitle: Asking your host about PHP is only step one.
wordpressSecurity.whyText: Your hosting provider or server administrator typically applies the PHP patches. You can ask them directly about the patch status at no cost. The paid package goes further: WordPress and plugin versions, backups, user access, login safeguards, carefully controlled routine updates and follow-up checks.
wordpressSecurity.serviceIntro: Six practical checks and actions, tailored to the site's condition and the defined launch-package scope.

features.title: PHP & hosting patch check

features.title: Regression checks & summary

wordpressSecurity.scopeText: The offer covers one standard WordPress site and up to 3 hours of work. It includes the agreed security review and compatible routine updates in that time. WooCommerce stores, incident response, malware cleanup, penetration testing, paid licenses, code fixes and complex upgrades are not included. If a site needs more work, we'll provide a separate quote before proceeding. No security audit can guarantee an invulnerable site.

faq.question: Why pay when I can simply ask my hosting provider?
faq.answer: You can—and should—ask them about the PHP patch status. That step is often straightforward. The paid package is for a broader WordPress review: versions, plugins, roles, backups, safeguards, routine updates and post-update checks.

faq.question: Does PHP2Shell affect every WordPress site?
faq.answer: No. Exposure depends on the PHP runtime and its patches. Some hosts backport fixes without changing the displayed version. We verify instead of guessing.

faq.question: Are all plugins updated for this price?
faq.answer: Compatible routine updates are included within the three-hour scope and only after approval and backup. Complex theme or plugin upgrades require a separate estimate.

faq.question: Does this include WooCommerce stores?
faq.answer: No. This package is for standard WordPress sites, including business websites, blogs, content portals and magazines. WooCommerce stores are excluded.

faq.question: How much does it cost?
faq.answer: The launch price is ILS 890 for one eligible standard WordPress site, covering up to three hours of agreed work. We confirm suitability and the final scope before any payment is required.

faq.question: Does this guarantee that my site is secure?
faq.answer: No. This is a targeted maintenance and security review, not penetration testing or incident forensics. We'll document findings and recommend any additional work.
